value.body: Once an aircraft maintenance engineer holds a basic DGCA licence, they still need training on a specific aircraft type — an Airbus A320 or an ATR 72, for example — before they can certify work on it. The type course covers that aircraft's systems, and the type is then endorsed on the licence.

items.label: Prerequisite
items.value: A DGCA AME licence (B1 or B2)
items.note: Plus the experience the endorsement asks for

items.label: DGCA-approved type-training organisations
items.source: Rajya Sabha reply, Ministry of Civil Aviation (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Usually through an employer: airlines and maintenance firms send their engineers on type courses for the aircraft they operate, often with a service bond. Self-funded type courses are possible, but the endorsement still needs practical experience on that type.

value.title: At a glance
items: A type endorsement ties you to operators that fly that aircraft.
Employer-sponsored training lowers cost but often comes with a bond period.
Engineers usually add further types over a career.
